gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-007 concerns a separate robustness and moving-sample-size quantifier problem in a joint-limit eigenpair theorem. It does not identify the abstract's overstatement of conditional subsequential spectral approximation, nor the nonzero weak-limit condition required to identify an exact eigenpair.

ISSUE-001 addresses finite-element dimension and nodal-basis construction. It contains no diagnosis that composition by an arbitrary flow fails to descend to L-infinity equivalence classes without null-set preservation.

ISSUE-007 concerns eigenpair selections and a diagonal-versus-uniform-in-M convergence claim. It does not diagnose the separate failure of the sampled-value quotient to define an empirical operator when sampling is non-injective.

Both entries identify the same failed population covariance identities under dictionary noise: the empirical Gram matrix is centered at G_N plus the noise covariance, with corresponding cross-covariance effects. Consequently the Bernstein centering and convergence-to-A_N guarantee are invalid without debiasing or revised biased-limit statements.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The noisy covariance estimator is not centered at the noiseless Gram/cross-covariance matrices because the dictionary noise contributes nonzero covariance and potentially cross-covariance. Thus increasing sample size does not remove the resulting asymptotic bias, and the claimed convergence and error guarantees around A_N do not follow.

component_coverage.gold_component: Dictionary noise changes the population covariance identities, so the empirical matrices are centered at perturbed matrices rather than G_N and C_N.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly computes the nonzero noise covariance contribution, notes that the summands are not centered, and explains why the concentration inference is unjustified.

component_coverage.gold_component: The resulting fixed-noise estimator has a nonvanishing asymptotic bias and does not converge arbitrarily closely to A_N under the stated one-batch setup.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the biased limiting operator, identifies the false arbitrarily-small A_N guarantee and dependent results, and proposes biased-limit reformulation or explicit debiasing machinery.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 recalculates the probability of a single 2N-dimensional Gaussian noise event and finds the stated chi-square degrees of freedom wrong. It does not identify the distinct conversion error that the joint truncation event has probability p-tilde_N^M rather than p-tilde_N.

Both entries identify the invalid use of pointwise strong projection convergence at the varying vector A f_{N_i} to infer norm convergence of (I-P_{F_{N_i}})A f_{N_i}. Both also recognize the valid fixed-test-vector pairing repair, which preserves the eigenfunction conclusion.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Pointwise convergence of the projections for each fixed test vector does not imply uniform or norm convergence when the argument A f_{N_i} varies with i. The proof must move the projection to a fixed g and establish only the paired scalar-product convergence.

component_coverage.gold_component: The projection assumption is pointwise for fixed vectors and cannot justify norm convergence applied to the varying sequence A f_{N_i}.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes fixed-vector convergence from the varying argument A f_{N_i}, supplies the l2 counterexample, and states that the asserted norm convergence does not follow.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof is repaired by testing against each fixed g and moving the self-adjoint projection onto g, rather than asserting norm convergence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same paired estimate with boundedness of A f_{N_i} and convergence of the projection on fixed g, and states that this restores the theorem.
